name: Matcha Pancakes

cookwares.name: 12-inch nonstick skillet or a well-seasoned cast iron or carbon steel skillet

ingredients.name: mixed berries, cut into bite-size pieces if needed
unsalted butter, melted, plus more for cooking as needed

instructions.primary_message: For the Macerated Berries: In a medium bowl, combine the berries and granulated sugar and toss until evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate until the berries release their juices and form a syrup, at least 1 hour or up to overnight,
For the Pancakes: In a large mixing bowl, sift together flour, sugar, matcha powder, baking powder, and salt, then whisk to combine.

When ready to cook, add buttermilk and egg to dry ingredients. In a large nonstick skillet, melt butter over medium heat, then pour it into the bowl (leave a light coating of butter in skillet and set aside). Whisk gently until just combined (the batter should remain lumpy, with just a few streaks of flour). Let batter sit for 10 to 15 minutes before cooking.

Return now-empty skillet to medium heat. To test the temperature of skillet, drop 1 tablespoon batter in center of skillet. If pancake is pale golden brown after 1 minute, skillet is ready. If it is too light or too dark, adjust heat accordingly.

Using 1/4-cup dry measuring cup or ice cream scoop, portion batter into skillet in 3 places, leaving even spacing between portions. Use the back of a measuring cup or a spoon to gently spread batter into a 4-inch round. Cook until bubbles on surface are just beginning to break, edges are set, and bottom sides are golden brown, 2 to 4 minutes.

Using a thin, wide spatula, flip pancakes and continue to cook until the second sides are golden brown, 1 to 3 minutes longer. Transfer to a plate and serve. (Alternatively, transfer cooked pancakes to a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet and hold warm in a 200℉; 93℃ oven until ready to serve.) Repeat with remaining batter, using additional butter as needed.

To Whip the Crème Fraîche: In a medium bowl, combine the crème fraîche and confectioners’ sugar. Using a whisk or an electric mixer, beat until the mixture thickens and holds soft peaks. Take care not to over-whip; the texture should remain smooth and light. Set aside or refrigerate until ready to serve.

To Serve: Stack individual portions of pancakes and spoon macerated berries over top, letting the juices run over the sides. Finish with a generous dollop of whipped crème fraîche. Serve with extra whipped crème fraîche on the side.

description: These fluffy matcha pancakes pair herbal green tea with sweet macerated berries and tangy whipped crème fraîche for a colorful brunch.
notes: Notes: Look for a good-quality, culinary-grade matcha with a robust flavor suited to cooking and baking; there’s no need to splurge on an expensive ceremonial matcha for this recipe. Since matcha begins to lose its vibrant color and flavor after it’s ground and exposed to air, buy it from a reputable tea shop, Japanese market, well-stocked supermarket, or online retailer with good turnover, preferably in a small, tightly sealed package. Look for matcha with a fresh green color rather than dull yellow or brown tones, and store it airtight in the refrigerator after opening.
author: Qi Ai
